prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: COc1cccc(-c2ccc(Nc3cc(=O)n(O)c(=O)[nH]3)cc2)c1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL247

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of HIV1 reverse transcriptase RNaseH activity using 3'-fluorescein/5'-Dabcyl labeled HTS-1 substrate
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of polymerase activity of HIV1 reverse transcriptase using poly(rA)-oligo(dT)16 and [3H]-TTP incubated for 20 mins by liquid scintillation spectrometry
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call":"NOT_COMMENSURABLE","confidence":0.98,"error_class":"assay_method","reason":"The assays measure distinct catalytic functions of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase—RNase H cleavage versus polymerase activity—so a function-selective inhibitor can yield IC50 values differing by more than 1 log unit."}
